{{2026 Indian Premier League Teams|main=y}}

The '''2026 Indian Premier League''', also known as '''IPL 19''' and branded as '''TATA IPL 2026''', was the 19th edition of the [[Indian Premier League]], a professional [[Twenty20]] [[cricket]] league. The tournament featured 10 teams competing in 74 matches from 28 March to 31 May across 13 venues.

Defending champions [[Royal Challengers Bengaluru]] defeated [[Gujarat Titans]] by 5 wickets in [[2026 Indian Premier League final|the final]] to secure their second consecutive IPL title. They became the first franchise to win the IPL and the [[2026 Women's Premier League (cricket)|Women's Premier League]] in the same year. [[Vaibhav Sooryavanshi]] of [[Rajasthan Royals]] scored the most runs (776) while [[Kagiso Rabada]] of Gujarat took the most wickets (29). Sooryavanshi was also named the most valuable player of the tournament.

== Background ==
The [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL) is a professional [[Twenty20]] (T20) [[cricket]] league, organised by the [[Board of Control for Cricket in India]] (BCCI). It has been held annually since the [[2008 Indian Premier League|first edition in 2008]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indian Premier League |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Indian-Premier-League |access-date=16 December 2025 |website=[[Britannica.com]] |language=en-uk|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250317155833/https://www.britannica.com/topic/Indian-Premier-League|archive-date=17 March 2025|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Royal Challengers Bengaluru]] were the defending champions, having won their maiden title in the [[2025 Indian Premier League|previous season]] after defeating [[Punjab Kings]] in the [[2025 Indian Premier League final|final]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-06-03 |title=RCB and Virat Kohli end 18-year wait for IPL glory with six-run defeat of Punjab Kings |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2025/jun/03/rcb-and-virat-kohli-end-18-year-wait-for-ipl-glory-with-six-run-defeat-of-punjab-kings |access-date=2025-12-23 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

=== Format ===
Each team played once against the teams in their group and twice against the teams in the other group. After the [[#League stage|group stage]], the top four teams, based on aggregate points, advanced to the [[#Playoffs|playoffs]]. In this stage, the top two teams competed with each other (in a match titled "[[#Qualifier 1|Qualifier 1]]"), as did the remaining two teams (in a match titled "[[#Eliminator|Eliminator]]"). While the winner of the Qualifier 1 directly qualified for the final match, the losing team had another chance to qualify for the final match by competing against the winning team of the Eliminator (in a match titled "[[#Qualifier 2|Qualifier 2]]"). The winner of this subsequent Qualifier 2 advanced to the final match. Teams were seeded into groups based on the number of titles they had won.<ref name="sch2">{{Cite web |first=Nagraj |last=Gollapudi |title=Mumbai to face CSK and RCB twice as IPL releases full league stage schedule |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-announces-full-league-stage-schedule-1529214 |access-date=27 March 2026 |date=26 March 2026 |publisher=[[Cricinfo|ESPNcricinfo]] |language=en |archive-date=27 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260327093618/https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-announces-full-league-stage-schedule-1529214 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="faq">{{Cite web |first=Hemant |last=Brar |title=IPL 2026 FAQs: New venue, big trades, and the million dollar Thala question |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2026-faqs-new-venues-big-trades-and-the-age-old-dhoni-question-1529084 |access-date=27 March 2026 |date=25 March 2026 |publisher=[[Cricinfo|ESPNcricinfo]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=IPL 2023 to be played from March 31 to May 28 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2023-to-begin-on-march-31-1359430 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250805213000/https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2023-to-begin-on-march-31-1359430 |archive-date=5 August 2025 |access-date=2026-03-27 |publisher=[[Cricinfo|ESPNcricinfo]] |language=en |url-status=live}}</ref>

The [[Indian Premier League#Organization|IPL Governing Council]] had initially announced that the IPL would expand to 84 matches for 2026 and 2027,<ref>{{Cite web |title=IPL 2025: No increase in the number of matches as BCCI wary of India's workload |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2025-with-player-workload-in-mind-no-increase-in-number-of-matches-played-1452783 |access-date=2024-10-01 |publisher=[[Cricinfo|ESPNcricinfo]] |language=en |archive-date=25 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250525221102/https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2025-with-player-workload-in-mind-no-increase-in-number-of-matches-played-1452783 |url-status=live}}</ref> with it expected to expand to 94 matches from 2028 onwards with the return of the complete [[double round-robin]] format that was used until 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arun Dhumal hints at expanded 94-match IPL in 2028 but without new teams |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-could-expand-to-94-matches-in-2028-with-csk-dc-mi-rcb-kkr-gt-pbks-srh-rr-and-lsg-as-the-ten-teams-1483410 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250429015210/https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-could-expand-to-94-matches-in-2028-with-csk-dc-mi-rcb-kkr-gt-pbks-srh-rr-and-lsg-as-the-ten-teams-1483410 |archive-date=29 April 2025 |access-date=2025-12-23 |publisher=[[Cricinfo|ESPNcricinfo]] |language=en |url-status=live}}</ref> However, the number of matches was kept as 74 for one more edition as it was in the previous four seasons.<ref>{{cite web |title=IPL 2026 Full Schedule Release: BCCI Confirms 74-Game Format |url=https://news.abplive.com/sports/cricket/bcci-ipl-2026-full-schedule-release-no-expansion-to-84-matches-full-fixtures-expected-shortly-1832535 |work=[[ABP Live]] |date=23 March 2026 |access-date=31 March 2026}}</ref>

|url=https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/bangladesh-bans-ipl-broadcast-in-another-retaliatory-move/article70473655.ece |access-date=2026-01-06 |work=[[The Hindu]] |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X |archive-date=5 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260105165042/https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/bangladesh-bans-ipl-broadcast-in-another-retaliatory-move/article70473655.ece |url-status=live}}</ref> Following the [[2026 Bangladeshi general election]], the newly elected government clarified that the broadcast of the IPL is not banned in their country anymore.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bangladesh opens door to IPL broadcast |url=https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/138165/bangladesh-opens-door-to-ipl-broadcast-cricbuzzcom |publisher=[[Cricbuzz]] |date=28 March 2026 |access-date=27 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Bangladesh clears IPL broadcast; government lifts restrictions |url=https://newsonair.gov.in/bangladesh-clears-ipl-broadcast-government-lifts-restrictions/ |work=News on Air |date=28 March 2026 |access-date=30 May 2026}}</ref>

=== Marketing ===
The [[Tata Group]] renewed their contract as the title sponsors of the IPL for a tenure of 5 years (2024–2028) for {{INRConvert|2500|c}}.<ref>{{cite news|title=TATA Group secures title sponsorship rights for IPL 2024-28|website=[[IPLT20.com]]|url=https://www.iplt20.com/news/3986/tata-group-secures-title-sponsorship-rights-for-ipl-2024-28|access-date=1 March 2024|date=20 January 2024|archive-date=21 February 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240221053306/https://www.iplt20.com/news/3986/tata-group-secures-title-sponsorship-rights-for-ipl-2024-28|url-status=live}}</ref> The advertising campaign for the 2026 IPL consisted of 27 sponsors including – [[Google AI Mode]], Campa Energy, [[Havells|Havells & Lloyd]], [[Aditya Birla Group|Birla Opus]], [[Hero MotoCorp]] and [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-03-26 |title=IPL 2026 advertisement gold rush: JioStar locks in 27 sponsors, big tech to FMCG pile in |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/media/entertainment/media/ipl-2026-advertisement-gold-rush-jiostar-locks-in-27-sponsors-big-tech-to-fmcg-pile-in/articleshow/129818441.cms |access-date=2026-05-07 |work=[[The Economic Times]] |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

=== Broadcasting ===
[[JioStar]]'s [[Star Sports (India)|Star Sports]] and [[JioHotstar]], held the television and digital  rights respectively, for the remainder of the 2023–2027 cycle.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McCaskill |first=Steve |date=2025-12-08 |title=JioStar seeks exit from US$3bn ICC cricket deal |url=https://www.sportspro.com/news/broadcast-ott/jiostar-icc-cricket-india-rights-deal-december-2025/ |access-date=2025-12-23 |website=[[SportsPro]] |language=en-GB |quote=JioStar also owns the domestic broadcast and streaming rights to the IPL [...] |archive-date=8 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251208131607/https://www.sportspro.com/news/broadcast-ott/jiostar-icc-cricket-india-rights-deal-december-2025/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In the opening weekend of the season which included two matches, linear television reported 7.84 million viewership, with an 18.8% drop in the average television viewership rating compared to last season, while JioHotstar reported 515 million viewership, with a 26% increase in total watch time to 32.6 billion minutes.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-04 |title=IPL 2026 Viewership slump: Linear TV ratings drop 18.8%, advertiser participation declines by 31% |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/sports/ipl-2026-viewership-slump-linear-tv-ratings-drop-18-percent-advertiser-participation-falls-31-percent/4231472/ |access-date=2026-05-07 |work=[[The Financial Express (India)|The Financial Express]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Menon |first=Balaram |date=2026-04-02 |title=IPL 2026 opening weekend shatters viewership records |url=https://gulfnews.com/sport/cricket/ipl/ipl-2026-opens-to-massive-audiences-setting-new-engagement-benchmarks-1.500493910 |access-date=2026-05-07 |work=[[Gulf News]] |language=en}}</ref>

=== Personnel changes ===
{{Main|List of 2026 Indian Premier League personnel changes}}
The franchises were required to submit their retention lists before 15 November 2025,<ref name="TOI">{{Cite news |date=2025-11-12 |title=IPL 2026 retention rules explained: How many players can a franchise retain or release before auction? |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/top-stories/ipl-2026-retention-rules-explained-how-many-players-can-a-franchise-retain-or-release-before-auction/articleshow/125275371.cms |access-date=2025-12-23 |work=[[The Times of India]] |issn=0971-8257 |archive-date=13 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251113035257/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/top-stories/ipl-2026-retention-rules-explained-how-many-players-can-a-franchise-retain-or-release-before-auction/articleshow/125275371.cms |url-status=live}}</ref> and a total of 173 players were retained ahead of the auction.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TATA IPL 2026 Player Retentions Announced |url=https://www.iplt20.com/news/4247/tata-ipl-2026-player-retentions-announced |access-date=23 December 2025 |website=[[IPLT20.com]]}}</ref> The auction was held on 16 December 2025 in [[Abu Dhabi]], United Arab Emirates<ref>{{cite web |access-date=15 December 2025 |title=IPL auction set to take place on December 16 in Abu Dhabi |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2026-auction-to-take-place-on-december-16-in-abu-dhabi-1510968 |publisher=[[Cricinfo|ESPNcricinfo]] |archive-date=5 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260105022626/https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2026-auction-to-take-place-on-december-16-in-abu-dhabi-1510968 |url-status=live}}</ref> with the auction purse for each franchise set at {{INRConvert|125|c}}.<ref name="retain1">{{Cite web |title=IPL 2026: How the squads stack up ahead of the auction |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2026-how-the-squads-stack-up-1511304 |access-date=23 December 2025 |publisher=[[Cricinfo|ESPNcricinfo]] |archive-date=16 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251116181308/https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2026-how-the-squads-stack-up-1511304 |url-status=live}}</ref> A total of 1,355 players registered for the auction, of which 369 players were shortlisted and 156 were featured in the auction and 77 were sold in the auction.<ref name="sold1">{{ESPNcricinfo 2|auction-sub|id=ipl-2026-auction-1515016|sub=sold players|event=2026 IPL auction|access-date=20 May 2026|dynamic=n|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260107180511/https://www.espncricinfo.com/auction/ipl-2026-auction-1515016/sold-players|archive-date=7 January 2026}}</ref><ref name="sold2">{{Cite web |title=IPL 2026 player list - full squads of each team |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/ipl-2026-teams-squads-list-player-prices |access-date=23 December 2025 |website=[[Olympics.com]]}}</ref><ref name=unsold/> [[Cameron Green]] became the most expensive overseas player and the third most expensive player in the history of the IPL when he was bought by Kolkata for {{INRConvert|25.20|c}}.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IPL auction 2026: Australia's Cameron Green becomes most expensive overseas player in tournament's history |url=https://www.skysports.com/cricket/news/12040/13484111/ipl-auction-2026-australias-cameron-green-becomes-most-expensive-overseas-player-in-tournaments-history |access-date=23 December 2025|work=[[Sky Sports]]}}</ref> [[Prashant Veer]] and [[Kartik Sharma]] became the joint-most expensive uncapped players in the history of the IPL when they were both bought by [[Chennai Super Kings]] for {{INRConvert|14.20|c}} each.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Who are Kartik Sharma and Prashant Veer - the costliest uncapped buys? |url=https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/136917/who-are-kartik-sharma-and-prashant-veer-the-costliest-uncapped-buys-cricbuzzcom |access-date=23 December 2025|publisher=[[Cricbuzz]]}}</ref> The 79 unsold players included players such as [[Jake Fraser-McGurk]], [[Jonny Bairstow]], [[Daryl Mitchell (New Zealand cricketer)|Daryl Mitchell]], [[Devon Conway]], [[Alzarri Joseph]], [[Gus Atkinson]], [[Deepak Hooda]] and [[Karn Sharma]].<ref name=unsold>{{Cite web |title=Unsold players at IPL 2026 auction: Jake Fraser-McGurk, Deepak Hooda among big names - get full list |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/ipl-2026-auction-unsold-player-list-indian-premier-league |access-date=23 December 2025|website=[[Olympics.com]]}}</ref>

== Venues ==
The league stage was played at 13 stadiums across India. 12 venues from the previous season returned as respective home grounds with HPCA Cricket Stadium and [[Assam Cricket Association Stadium|ACA Cricket Stadium]] as secondary home venues for three Punjab Kings matches and three [[Rajasthan Royals]] matches respectively.<ref name="sch1"/><ref name="sch2"/> [[ACA–VDCA Cricket Stadium]] was dropped as [[Delhi Capitals]] secondary home venue<ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-03-11 |title=IPL first phase schedule out: No matches in Vizag |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Visakhapatnam/ipl-first-phase-schedule-out-no-matches-in-vizag/article70731748.ece |access-date=2026-05-07 |work=[[The Hindu]] |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref> while [[Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh International Cricket Stadium|Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh Stadium]] which had previously served as secondary home venue for [[Delhi Daredevils]] until 2016, was added as secondary home venue for two Royal Challengers Bengaluru matches.<ref name="faq"/><ref name="sch2"/><ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-01-13 |title=Treat for Kohil fans: Raipur to host 2 RCB matches this IPL |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/raipur/treat-for-kohil-fans-raipur-to-host-2-rcb-matches-this-ipl/articleshow/126508201.cms |access-date=2026-05-07 |work=[[The Times of India]] |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> The opening match was played at M. Chinnaswamy Stadium.<ref name="sch1"/> The playoffs were played at HPCA Cricket Stadium and Maharaja Yadavindra Singh Stadium with the final at Narendra Modi Stadium.<ref name="pos3"/>
